modules.name: Layer manifest and provenance schema
modules.design_question: What single manifest lets any module find, verify, cache, credit and datum-check a layer, and trace each value to a source, without opening the data?
modules.method: Extend Vista's release-manifest (per-file bytes, sha256) into manifest.json 'vcm-layers/1' with a JSON Schema. One record per layer: id, theme, version; source {publisher, dataset_id, url, retrieved, source_modified}; licence {id, attribution, share_alike, redistribution}; crs {horizontal datum, epoch, EPSG; vertical {datum, epsg|null, z_offset_m, basis}}; geometry; lod; accuracy; vintage; bbox; count; fields; files [{path, role, format, bytes, sha256, content_type, range_safe}]; derived_from; build {script, commit}; modules_using; status. File paths are content-addressed (layers/<id>/<sha256[:12]>.<ext>); only manifest.json keeps a fixed name, because Pages caches every file for 10 minutes. Policy documents (council reports, guideline PDFs) get source records with URL, retrieved date, sha256 and page count. CI rejects: missing licence, datum or CRS; hash, byte or path-hash mismatch; file over cap; an ODbL ancestor in derived_from without share_alike; range_safe true without a passing browser probe; GeoParquet metadata containing '-dev'. Modules declare requires:[layer ids]; the registry computes what to fetch. Rule: every coordinate and height traces to a survey or open-data file; GPT-6 Astra may draft code and text only.
modules.human_judgment: Decide which layers ship in the core bundle; confirm attribution wording and datum statements with each publisher; choose which policy documents the registry tracks.

modules.name: Storage formats and tiling
modules.design_question: Which format and tiling per layer minimises bytes yet lets the browser load only what the current view needs, while keeping absolute heights for cone tests?
modules.method: Choose format by access pattern. Points and tables (trees, heritage, stations, parcel and tax attributes): GeoParquet 1.1 with an explicit geometry column, crs as PROJJSON, bbox covering column, Hilbert sort, zstd; read with hyparquet, passing byteLength from the manifest. Display polygons (parcels, footprints, zoning, parks): PMTiles v3 MVT, about z10-z16 with overzoom; keep the same data as GeoParquet for analysis. LOD1: store footprint plus absolute elevations (z_ground_m, z_roof_max_m, z_roof_p50_m), vintage and flags, never baked meshes; derive height_m = z_roof - z_ground for display only; MapLibre fill-extrusion takes height and base in metres. Mark LOD1.3 where tops differ by more than about 2 m. Terrain and canopy rasters: quantised uint16 decimetres or uint8 half-metres as WebP/PNG tiles in PMTiles, or COG, datum in manifest. Hand-modelled meshes: glTF with KHR_mesh_quantization and EXT_meshopt_compression. 3D Tiles only if Cesium is adopted (ellipsoidal heights). View cones: analytic parameters, not meshes. Point clouds: link NRCan COPC, never mirror. Metric work EPSG:3157. Publish a measured size table before committing any layer.
modules.human_judgment: Choose which layers need analysis-grade geometry (Parquet) versus display-only tiles; accept lossy simplification for far context buildings; set the change-detection threshold for 2015 footprints.

modules.name: GitHub hosting, size budgets and range/compression
modules.design_question: How do we host a multi-layer open dataset within GitHub limits while keeping range-read formats working in every target browser?
modules.method: Limits (docs): Pages site 1 GB, deploy timeout 10 minutes, bandwidth soft 100 GB/month; the 10 builds/hour soft limit does not apply to custom Actions workflows. Git warns at 50 MiB, blocks at 100 MiB; releases 2 GiB per file, 1,000 assets, no CORS; LFS free 10 GiB and unusable with Pages. Measured 21 Oct 2026 on the team's Pages site: max-age=600, ACAO *, no Access-Control-Expose-Headers; octet-stream and JSON are gzip-encoded for clients that ask. Chromium 152 sends identity when Range is present: fetch returned 206 with raw size and no encoding, so ranges work. A browser HEAD returns the gzip Content-Length (2,383,874 versus 9,722,568 raw), which misleads readers that size files from HEAD. Plan: (1) build in CI, deploy with upload-pages-artifact; (2) release zips for citation, never browser delivery; (3) Playwright probe in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit per extension: 206, raw total, magic bytes; curl is diagnostic only; (4) content-addressed paths, previous version kept one cycle; (5) pass byteLength from the manifest; (6) fallback: 1 km shards or a CORS object store.
modules.human_judgment: If Firefox or WebKit probes fail, decide between sharding and a CORS-enabled object store (adds an account and possible cost).

modules.name: Local cache and layer subscription
modules.design_question: How do tools subscribe to layers, stay fresh as open data and policy change, and work offline with minimal bandwidth?
modules.method: Subscription is manifest plus versions. The client fetches manifest.json (Pages caches it 10 minutes), compares each layer's version and sha256 with its cache, and downloads only changed content-addressed files, so a stale manifest and a fresh file cannot mix. Browser cache: Cache Storage or OPFS keyed by sha256; keep current and previous. Desktop/Python: %LOCALAPPDATA%/vancouver-context/<layer>/<version>/ with a lock file. Modules call registry.require(['cov-public-trees']) and receive a handle plus attribution; they re-render on a layer-updated event. A weekly GitHub Action reads each portal dataset's data_processed, rebuilds changed layers, carries the previous version's files forward one cycle, validates and deploys. The same job re-hashes tracked policy PDFs (Public Views Guidelines, Solar Access Guidelines, City-wide Design and Development Guidelines) and opens an issue when a hash or amendment date changes. Offline mode serves cached layers and shows source dates. Optional live fallback: City portal exports send Access-Control-Allow-Origin * (HEAD-tested), but rate limits are unverified, so never depend on them at runtime.
modules.human_judgment: Set refresh policy per layer and decide whether students may enable live portal fallback.

modules.name: Licence, attribution and share-alike
modules.design_question: Which licence and attribution does each layer carry, and how do we keep ODbL share-alike from spreading to other layers, including inherited Vista assets?
modules.method: Licence register keyed by layer. OGL-Vancouver (v1.0, based on OGL-BC 2.0), OGL-Metro Vancouver (v1.0), OGL-BC 2.0 and OGL-Canada 2.0 allow commercial use, modification and redistribution with attribution; default statement 'Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Vancouver' (same pattern for Metro Vancouver). Exclusions: personal information, third-party rights, official marks; no endorsement. OSM and Overture buildings are ODbL. Per the OSMF Collective Database guideline, each feature type and region must be all-OSM or all-non-OSM with no cross-references, else the merge is ODbL. Keep ODbL layers in separate files with share_alike=true; rendered PNG/PDF are Produced Works but the database must stay available. Do not merge OSM heights into City footprints. Audit inherited Vista assets: OSM coastline and water clip the terrain; shoreline, water and extension buildings are OSM; the supplied Rhino model was built from 2022 OSM data per its manifest. Flag them ODbL or rebuild coast and water from City LiDAR class 5. TransLink data is permission-based, legend required, revocable: fetch optionally, never mirror. BC Assessment bulk data is not open: use the City tax report. Code MIT or Apache-2.0; NOTICE generated from the manifest.
modules.human_judgment: Ask the City and Metro Vancouver whether the default attribution suffices; decide whether to include any ODbL layer at all or rebuild coast and water from non-OSM sources.

modules.name: Vertical datum and CRS registry
modules.design_question: How do heights from CGVD28, CGVD28GVRD, CGVD2013, EGM96 and ellipsoid layers, and portal lon/lat labelled WGS84, stay comparable for cone and airspace tests?
modules.method: Every z-bearing file declares z_ref. Known: City LiDAR 2013 CGVD28 and 2018/2022 CGVD28GVRD (Metro Vancouver geoid HTMVBC00); NRCan HRDEM CGVD2013 in EPSG:3979 COGs; Vista SRTM EGM96; 3D Tiles WGS84 ellipsoid; City 2013 DEM zip and YVR 'above sea level' not named; cone heights 'geodetic' with the datum unnamed (council reports give only NAD 1983 UTM 10N corner coordinates). EPSG: 5713 CGVD28; 9245 CGVD2013a(2010), replacing 6647; 4979; 3157; 4617. Horizontal: portal 'WGS84' lon/lat equal NAD83(CSRS) values (LiDAR tile corners project to round kilometres; a parcel vertex matches the City's UTM corner within 0.113 m), so label them NAD83(CSRS); EPSG lists NAD83(CSRS) to WGS 84 transformations of 1 m and 2 m accuracy, so mixing with GNSS, web imagery or 3D Tiles needs a declared transform. Vertical: estimate z_offset_m by differencing NRCan HRDEM VILLE_VANCOUVER (acquired 2013-02-19, CGVD2013) against City 2013 LiDAR GeoTIFFs (flown February 2013, CGVD28) on bare ground. Keep +0.15 m only as a labelled placeholder. Transforms apply on load, never inside source files. Cone results carry 'cone datum unconfirmed' until the City replies.
modules.effort: est. 3-4 days including the offset study
modules.human_judgment: Confirm with the City which datum cone geodetic heights use and whether 'measured from' a corner means absolute elevation, before choosing the canonical datum.

modules.name: Trees and canopy layers
modules.design_question: How do we store street trees and canopy compactly while stating height and crown uncertainty honestly?
modules.method: Trees: build cov-public-trees from the portal Parquet export (10,358,425 B raw). Keep asset_id, genus/species dictionary ids, diameter_cm (uint16, 0.1 cm), height class and position (0.1 m, EPSG:3157). Drop or flag 477 zero diameters, 3 zero heights and 1 null geometry. height_m has 84 distinct values but ten classes hold 95.6% of trees (4.6 to 32.0 m); these equal 15 to 105 ft in 10 ft steps, so label them 'recorded class value (inferred 10 ft bins)', uncertainty about plus or minus 1.5 m, never 'measured'. Crown width is not supplied: estimate from diameter and genus (team assumption; calibrate on LiDAR). Canopy: derive a canopy height model from City LiDAR 2022 (class 4, DSM minus DTM) at 2 m, uint8 half-metre tiles; 2013 and 2018 LiDAR give change checks; Metro Vancouver 2020 5 m land cover is the regional cross-check. Private trees exist only in the CHM. Prototype: 184,267 valid trees pack to 874,891 B (4.75 B each) with zlib-9. Instance one low-poly crown per genus.
modules.human_judgment: Decide the acceptable crown model and whether to request City canopy polygons.

modules.name: Future layers: land value, zoning, heritage, transit, traffic, view-cone parameters, shadow, airspace
modules.design_question: How do land value, zoning, heritage, transit, traffic, cone parameters, shadow-sensitive spaces and airspace plug into the store without new geometry, and which are safe to use in warnings?
modules.method: Store each future layer as attribute-light tables keyed to existing geometry. Land value: aggregate the 2026 tax report (228,935 folios) by land_coordinate (sum land and improvement values, count folios, keep legal_type) and dissolve parcels by tax_coord before joining; mark strata sums. Zoning: keep zoning_district and cd_1_number; no height field. Heritage: category, evaluationgroup, status. Transit: 20 unique stations; add Broadway Subway as 'planned' (BC government: fall 2027). Traffic: locations only; volumes unresolved. View-cone parameters: store policy-sourced reference corners and geodetic heights with page citations (cov-public-views-params). Shadow-sensitive spaces: parks, schools and the Council Table 1 list with rule parameters (equinox, 10 am to 4 pm). Airspace: store SOR/80-902 parameters only, no surface geometry; layer 'unconfirmed', excluded from compliance warnings until Plan BC 1280 and the 2026 proposed-limit maps are obtained.
